description: Class-A1 filesystem-spelling equivalence on the Write/Edit channel (trailing-dot/space, NTFS ADS, traversable directory-stream). Sibling of BC-025 (which covered the NFKC/case-fold family). Windows strips trailing dots and spaces from path components (``.claude.`` and ``.claude `` both open ``.claude``), and resolves an NTFS alternate-data-stream suffix (``file::$DATA`` / ``file:streamname``) to the base file. The traversable directory stream ``dir::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`` is worse: ``tools/cc::$INDEX_ALLOCATION/hooks/write_guard.py`` opens the real hook file but leaves a colon on the DIRECTORY component, so a basename-only strip misses it. Pre-fix, ``_protected_zones`` exact-matched the un-stripped spelling and these landed in the protected zone while the string check missed -> ALLOWED. The fix: ``_fs_equiv(rel, *, all_components=True)`` strips per-component trailing ``.``/space + the ADS stream (split on first ``:``, plus ``::$DATA``/``::$INDEX_ALLOCATION``) on the input AND every set member, applied to ALL components for ``_is_protected`` (asymmetric: basename-only for ``_is_allowed`` so a forged directory component can never widen the allowlist). This is the regression gate that keeps the spelling-equivalence class fixed.
